## ESG评估 ESG Assessment

Orrin holds no licence it can lose, but four inputs to its value case sit outside its control before 2027: a wage floor a California court reopened, a robotics tariff due by 2027-04-26, a licence test on 2027-12-31 and a California driver requirement AB 187 leaves in force. My judgement: the balance is negative for 2027 and positive after, and the inputs that decide it are conditions the company would have to meet, not risks a valuation absorbs. (S1, S126)

### The wage floor, not the robot, sets the price

The grower's alternative cost moved against Orrin in 2026. The skill-based wage floor effective 2026-08-03 puts California's entry-level adverse effect wage rate at $16.45 an hour against the $19.97 Farm Labor Survey rate that governed to 2025-10-01 — a 17.6% cut — with the experienced level at $18.71; Florida fell from $16.23 to $12.47 and $15.06. On the deck's quarter-acre per picker-day, one pass over an acre costs $526 of hand labour at Level I and $599 at Level II: $21,056–$23,949 an acre over a 40-pass season. At $9,500 a robot-season over 3.5 acres the robot is $2,714 an acre, 11%–13% of that, and $4,714 at the 2027 list price, so price is not what stops adoption: Grower B cut from 22 to 14 robots while Grower E left over bruising. On 2026-08-26 a California district court held the October 2025 methodology unlawful on four grounds — skill tiers, housing, wage survey, primary-duty rule — ordered a replacement and warned of back wages. A higher California rate is more likely than not to apply in 2027, restoring most of the 17.6% cut and lifting the ceiling [S80, S81, S1].

### The rule that stands, and who is organised

The United Farm Workers, which won that case, will shape the rule. AB 187, the session's employment trailer bill, passed both houses on 2026-08-31 and was chaptered on 2026-09-18 as Chapter 256 without the Cal/OSHA amendment that would have let unpiloted machines work beside crews; the standard requiring a human driver in agricultural workplaces therefore stands through the 2027 season, and the Standards Board's advisory committee first meets on 2026-12-01 [S126, S124, S142, S82, S115, S1]. Both readings of that rule end the investment. The mechanism is asymmetric: if a technician satisfies the standard, the 1:8 ratio is the exposure and a 1:1 technician puts field service above the season price, which means the service margin fails; if the fleet cannot satisfy it, one citation stops the only revenue line. Material restriction or enforcement in 2027: 20%–25% probability, -70% to -90% of equity value — probability times impact, not probability alone. The restriction becomes acceptable only on three conditions, none met today: a counsel opinion that a technician satisfies the human-driver standard; a Cal/OSHA interpretation or an advisory-committee outcome confirming that reading; and field service at 1:8 or better. California overtime adds to the hand cost displaced; Florida's exposure is immigration enforcement.

### The robot crosses a border being re-priced

Orrin owns the fleet, so duty lands on its capital cost. USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico enter at 0%, non-qualifying robots at 10%: $3,300 on the $33,000 v4 bill of materials, 26% of the $12,700 renewal price and 85% of a robot-season's $3,900 gross profit. The Section 232 robotics proclamation of 2026-10-28 found a threat, imposed no duty and set a Commerce–USTR update within 180 days [S88, S89]. At 25% that is $8,250 a robot, or $2.48M against a $9.9M 2027 build budget. Whether the robot meets USMCA origin is not disclosed; metals duties of 50% apply even when it does.

### A licence with a cliff, and a statute nobody has checked

The licence costs 2.5% of net robot revenue with a $40,000 minimum — the floor binds in FY2026 at 5.6% of robots-as-a-service revenue — and falls to non-exclusive below 100 robots in commercial service on 2027-12-31, against 75 paid robot-seasons and a 64-robot fleet [S1, S85, S86]. A binary test with no cure is harsher than practice, where exclusive licences carry diligence milestones and cure periods. The plan clears the threshold; the cliff needs 72% slippage (20%–25% conversion risk). If either family was federally funded, 35 U.S.C. 204 requires the exclusive US licensee to manufacture substantially in the US, and Guadalajara assembles the grippers.

### Food safety is an equipment problem now

21 CFR Part 112 names mechanical harvesters as equipment, and 112.123 requires food-contact surfaces to be smooth, cleanable and cleaned and sanitised as necessary [S83, S92]. Picking into the clamshell makes the machine's interior a packing surface, and field-packed fruit reaches the consumer unwashed. No federal certificate exists and no FDA action on machine-harvested berries was found; the gate is a retailer audit and the penalty a delisting. ISO 18497-1:2024 sets design and verification requirements for autonomous agricultural machinery, is voluntary, and no assessment against it is disclosed.

### The social case is a product metric

Labour substitution is an asset only where labour supply binds, not where quality binds: the numbers that move a purchase are the 94% pick rate, 3.8% bruising and 86% uptime, on rows excluding plastic tunnels, standing water and slopes over 4%. No retailer standard or campaign aimed at machine-harvested strawberries was identified. Governance carries more weight: Tallis is noteholder, board observer, customer, contract manufacturer and investor; the COO's own company is paid for robot moves and night supervision; the independent board seat is vacant; and ARR includes letters of intent and a contract ending 2027-06-30. USAspending returns no award under the company's name against the Phase II award the deck describes [S91, S1].

Four records are requested — the H-2A files and wage table, the SBIR award, the USPTO assignment chain and licence, and the AB 187 text — so confidence is medium on tariff and licence exposure and low on food-safety compliance. For the investor, the factors change what a season is worth, not whether Orrin can sell one; the test they set is whether the three California conditions hold before the 2027 season.
